title: Relative derived tensor and canonical projection arrow on algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in [def-weil-size-convention], with module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the recorded small ringed models, their module equivalences, derived direct image and K-flat derived tensor $T_X$ [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus], ordinary tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] and its total left derivation $Lf^*$ [def-sfb-space-derived-tensor-pullback], shared derivation counit [def-sfb-space-derived-pullback], normalized derived adjunction [def-sfb-space-affine-hom-comparison], and normalized pullback tensor comparison [def-sfb-space-base-change-comparisons]. Define the ordinary relative balanced total tensor of complexes $P,Q$ by the signed direct-sum total of $P\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}f^*Q$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This presents $P\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}f^{-1}Q$ with its $\mathcal O_X$-action through $P$, via the ordinary mutually inverse balancing formulas $p\otimes(a\otimes q)\mapsto ap\otimes q$ and $p\otimes q\mapsto p\otimes(1\otimes q)$. After localization this bifunctor has a total left derived functor at pairs of quasi-isomorphisms. Define $B_f:D(\mathcal O_X)\times D(\mathcal O_Y)\to D(\mathcal O_X)$ to be that universal total left derived functor, retaining its counit to the ordinary relative tensor. There is a unique natural isomorphism $T_X(E,Lf^*G)\cong B_f(E,G)$ whose equation on every pair $P,Q$ of flat-term K-flat representatives is the shared pullback counit on $Q$ followed by the inverse of the recorded tensor representative comparison; its composite with the relative derived counit equals this map. Define $\pi_{f,E,G}:T_Y(Rf_*E,G)\to Rf_*T_X(E,Lf^*G)$ as the adjunct of the normalized pullback tensor comparison followed by the derived counit on $E$ tensored with the identity on $Lf^*G$. Define the relative projection arrow as $\pi_{f,E,G}$ followed by $Rf_*$ of the unique balanced comparison above. This arrow is natural in both arguments, with no boundedness, flatness, relative Tor, properness or quasi-compactness assumption.
